title: Split Shop into commands and a read view

task.text: `Shop` accepts orders and answers revenue questions from the same data.
Split it in two and keep `Shop.place`, `revenue` and `top` behaving exactly as now (`top` ranks by revenue, ties by name).

items: `OrderCommands` is the write side: `void handle(PlaceOrder)` validates (`IllegalArgumentException("amount")`, `IllegalStateException("duplicate <id>")`) and appends an `OrderPlaced` to `List<OrderPlaced> feed()`. It answers no queries.
`RevenueView` is the read side: `void catchUp(List<OrderPlaced> feed)` applies only events it has not seen, then `int revenue(String)` and `List<String> top(int)` answer from its own totals.
`Shop` only wires the two. `Messages.java` is read-only.

checks.title: top ranks by revenue, ties by name
A duplicate order id is rejected
OrderCommands handles commands and publishes a feed
The write side answers no queries
RevenueView is built from the feed alone
Shop keeps no data of its own

hints.text: There are two different jobs: deciding whether an order is allowed, and answering questions about totals. They want different shapes of data, so give each its own model.

`OrderCommands` keeps what it needs to reject duplicates plus the feed of `OrderPlaced` facts. `RevenueView` keeps `Map<String, Integer>` totals and a count of events already applied. `Shop` calls `handle`, then `catchUp(commands.feed())`.
